content.text:
Start working on Linear ticket eng-2228 by fetching its details and creating a dedicated git worktree.

## Steps

### 1. Validate input
- `eng-2228` should be a Linear ticket ID like `ENG-1271`. If missing or malformed, ask the user.

### 2. Fetch ticket details from Linear
- Use `mcp__linear-server__get_issue` with the issue ID `eng-2228`
- Extract: title, description, and `branchName` (Linear provides this)
- If the Linear tool is unavailable, ask the user for a branch name manually

### 3. Determine branch name
- Use the `branchName` field from Linear if available (it's already formatted correctly)
- Otherwise derive it: lowercase the ticket ID + hyphenated slug of the title
  - Example: `ENG-1271 Implement filter search` → `eng-1271-implement-filter-search`
  - Strip special characters, replace spaces with hyphens, truncate to ~60 chars

### 4. Create git worktree
Run these from the repo root (the main working directory, not an existing worktree):

```bash
# Fetch latest main so the worktree starts from up-to-date origin/main
git fetch origin main

# Check if branch already exists
git branch --list <branch-name>

# Check if worktree already exists
git worktree list | grep <branch-name>
```

- **If worktree already exists**: skip to step 5, just `cd` into `.claude/worktrees/<branch-name>`
- **If branch does NOT exist**: `git worktree add -b <branch-name> .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> origin/main`
- **If branch already exists but no worktree**: reset the branch to `origin/main` first, then add the worktree:
  ```bash
  git branch -f <branch-name> origin/main
  git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> <branch-name>
  ```

### 5. Enter the worktree
**Do NOT use the `EnterWorktree` tool** — it always creates a brand-new worktree and will duplicate the one you just created.

Instead, use `cd` to switch into the worktree directory:
```bash
cd .claude/worktrees/<branch-name>
```

All subsequent commands should run from this path.

### 6. Install dependencies and set up the worktree
After entering the worktree, run the following to bootstrap the environment:

```bash
pnpm install
```

This is required because worktrees share git objects but each needs its own `node_modules`.

### 6b. Copy .env files from the main repo into the worktree
`.env` files are gitignored, so each worktree needs its own copies. After `pnpm install`, copy all `.env` files (excluding `.env.example` files) from the main repo root into the matching relative paths in the worktree.

The main repo root is the working directory you were in before entering the worktree (e.g. `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph`).

Run:
```bash
# From the main repo root, find all .env files (not .env.example) and copy them into the worktree
find . -name ".env*" \
  -not -name ".env.example" \
  -not -path "./.git/*" \
  -not -path "./node_modules/*" \
  -not -path "./.claude/worktrees/*" \
  | while read f; do
      dest=".claude/worktrees/<branch-name>/$f"
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
      cp "$f" "$dest"
    done
```

Report which files were copied so the user can confirm.

### 7. Ask the user which app to start
Ask the user which app they want to run in dev mode. Common options:
- **Roam**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=none pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/roam dev`
- **Obsidian**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=local pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/obsidian dev`
- **None**: just set up the environment without starting a dev server

If the user says Roam, also switch the Roam dev symlink:
```bash
ln -sfn <worktree>/apps/roam/dist ~/roam-ext-dev
```
and remind them to reload the developer extension in Roam.

Run the chosen dev command in the background so the user can continue working.

**Dev server gotchas** (learned the hard way — don't rediscover these):

- The filter flag is `--filter`, not `--F`. Turbo 2.5.6 rejects `--F=roam` outright.
- Prefer `pnpm -C <abs-path> <app> dev` over `turbo dev --filter=<app>`. `turbo dev --filter=roam`
  also runs the `@repo/database#dev` dependency, which requires Docker Desktop plus an explicit
  `SUPABASE_USE_DB`; if Docker isn't running turbo fails the *entire* run even though the app
  itself built fine. Going through `pnpm -C` skips the dependency graph.
- `SUPABASE_USE_DB` must be one of `local | branch | production | none | implicit`
  (see `packages/database/src/dbDotEnv.mjs`). Use `none` for work that doesn't touch the database.
- **Always bake the absolute worktree path into the command.** The Bash tool's cwd resets to the
  main repo between calls, so a backgrounded `pnpm --filter roam dev` with no path silently builds
  the *main repo's* `dist` — not the worktree the symlink points at. `pnpm -C <abs-path>` makes the
  path intrinsic to the command so it can't be dropped.
- After starting, verify before reporting success: confirm the log says `built with 0 errors` **and**
  that `<worktree>/apps/roam/dist` has a fresh mtime. A background task that failed still returns a
  task ID.

### 8. Ingest any saved session context
The branch may have been worked on before (e.g. reset from an existing branch).
Check for recorded session context:

```bash
bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve
```

- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=yes`, **read the `CONTEXT_FILE`** and load it as working context
  (`Next step`, `Open questions`, `Key decisions`, `Dead ends`).
- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=no` or the command errors, continue — this is a fresh start.

### 9. Show context
After setup, display:
- Ticket ID and title
- Branch name you're on
- Brief description from the ticket (if available)
- Which app dev server is running (if any)
- If prior session context was found: its `TL;DR` and `Next step`
- A short "ready to work" confirmation
- Remind the user they can run `/checkpoint` to save session context before wrapping up

## ENG-2228 — Add link support to tldraw text shapes in Obsidian

**Branch:** `eng-2228-add-link-support-to-tldraw-text-shapes-in-obsidian` (from `origin/main` @ `476051456`)
**Worktree:** `.claude/worktrees/eng-2228-add-link-support-to-tldraw-text-shapes-in-obsidian`

**The ask:** Text shapes can't link to a page or URL, so a simplified canvas narrative can't open its detailed source. Geo shapes already have this. Reuse the geo-shape link code path — don't build a separate text-shape implementation.

**Done when:** text shapes expose the same **Edit link** action; add/edit/open/remove behaves and looks identical to geo; link survives close-and-reopen of the canvas; unit tests cover persistence and text-shape eligibility.

**Out of scope:** converting text shapes into Discourse Graph nodes, a page picker or new link format, links on other shape types.

**Environment:**
- `pnpm install` done; 11 `.env` files copied from the main repo (skills, packages/database ×5, website, roam, obsidian ×3)
- Obsidian dev server running in background (task `b2ac53f5m`) — `built with 0 errors`, mirrored to `~/Documents/testVault/.obsidian/plugins/discourse-graphs`

> **TL;DR** Code is written and statically verified (types, 233 tests, build, bundle grep) but has never been opened in Roam. The ticket's premise was wrong — there is no app-side geo link code to reuse; the real work was giving the text shape a `url` prop plus a migration.

## Goal / scope agreement
Ticket said "reuse the geo-shape link code path." There is no such code in `apps/roam` — the entire geo link feature is stock tldraw 2.4.6, gated on a duck-type check `'url' in shape.props` (`menu-hooks.ts:173`). `text` has no `url` prop, so the work is schema, not UI wiring. Once the prop exists, the context-menu item and `EditLinkDialog` light up for free because `uiOverrides.tsx` leaves `ContextMenu`, `ActionsMenu` and `Dialogs` at defaults.

## Key decisions
- **[2026-09-14] Store the link in `shape.props.url`, not `shape.meta`** — *Why:* matches the ticket, and the codebase already has a props-migration pattern (3 of the 5 existing migrations add props to shapes). *Rejected:* `shape.meta.url`, which needs no migration at all because `createShapeValidator` leaves meta as `T.jsonValue` — but it requires hand-rolling the menu item + dialog, i.e. exactly the "separate text-shape implementation" the ticket forbids. *Revisit if:* we ever need text links to survive an extension rollback.
- **[2026-09-14] Put the migration in `com.roam-research.discourse-graphs` v6, not `com.tldraw.shape.text` v3** — *Why:* our own namespace can't collide with a future tldraw release that bumps its text sequence. *Revisit if:* the sequence is ever split per shape type.
- **[2026-09-14] Backfill defensively (`if url === undefined`)** — *Why:* migration v3 originally assigned unconditionally and clobbered user values; fixed in PR #916 (your own). A test asserts double-application is a no-op.

## Dead ends
- `T.linkUrl.optional()` to avoid writing a migration — looked like it would work, but the eligibility gate is `'url' in props`, which is false when the key is absent. Old text shapes would silently never show Edit link while new ones would. A migration is mandatory, not a nicety.
- Reasoning about what happens to un-migrated shapes — had to be measured. Without the migration, `migrateStoreSnapshot` reports **success** and silently does nothing, then validation throws `At shape(type = text).props.url: Expected string, got undefined`, and `onValidationFailure` rethrows even at `phase === 'initialize'`. Failure mode is "canvas won't open", not a silent degrade.
- Importing tldraw's CJS bundle in `node -e` to check exports — hangs (pulls in React/DOM). Grep the `.d.ts` or copy an existing import from `DiscourseNodeUtil.tsx` instead.

## Constraints & preferences
- No dev server this session — user asked to go straight to planning, so nothing has been exercised in the real app.
- User pushed back twice on my recommendations and was right both times; the props-vs-meta call was only settled by looking at actual repo history rather than arguing from first principles.

## Gotchas / landmines
- The sync worker (`apps/tldraw-sync-worker/worker/TldrawDurableObject.ts`) builds its room schema from `defaultShapeSchemas` + `{}` entries for custom types. `{}` is fully permissive (`props ? T.object(props) : T.jsonValue`), but `text` gets real `textShapeProps` and would reject `url` — hence `"text"` is now appended to the `shapeType` query params in `TldrawCanvasCloudflareSync.tsx`. Side effect: server-side validation of *all* text props is now off.
- `[...defaultShapeUtils, ...customShapeUtils]` appears at **four** sites (`Tldraw.tsx`, `useRoamStore.ts`, `TldrawCanvasCloudflareSync.tsx`, `Export.tsx`). They must stay in sync or `Export.tsx` fails validating persisted data. Hence `baseShapeUtils.ts`.
- Registering both `TextShapeUtil` and a subclass throws *"defined more than once"* — it must be replaced in the list, not appended.
- Two React type copies in the tree: `TextShapeUtil.component`'s declared `JSX.Element` is nominally distinct from ours (`key` is `Key | null` vs `string | null`). Needs a cast; commented in the file.
- `createMigrationSequence` rejects a sequence that doesn't start at version 1 — v6 must be appended in place, never split into its own file.
- Downgrading the extension already breaks any canvas migrated past the installed version (`getMigrationsSince` → `Result.err('Incompatible schema?')`). This predates our change; don't treat it as newly introduced.

# ENG-2228 — Add link support to tldraw text shapes in Obsidian

## Context

Text shapes on the Obsidian tldraw canvas can't carry a link, so a simplified canvas narrative can't open the detailed source its text stands for. Geo shapes can.

**The ticket's premise is wrong, and ENG-2227 already confirmed it on the Roam side.** There is no app-side geo-link code to reuse — in `apps/obsidian` the entire link feature (the **Edit link** action, `EditLinkDialog`, the corner icon) is stock tldraw 3.14.2. Eligibility is duck-typed, not an allowlist:

```ts
// node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts:173 — useHasLinkShapeSelected
!!(shape && shape.type !== 'embed' && 'url' in shape.props && !shape.isLocked)
```

`TLGeoShape` declares `url`; `TLTextShape` does not. So this is a **schema change, not UI wiring**. Once `text` props carry `url`, the context-menu item and dialog light up for free — `CustomContextMenu.tsx:65` renders `<DefaultContextMenuContent />`, and there is no `actions` override anywhere in the app.

This plan mirrors the ENG-2227 Roam implementation (written, statically verified, not yet merged) so the two apps stay consistent. Roam's settled decisions carry over; the deltas are called out below.

## Decisions inherited from ENG-2227

- **Store the link in `shape.props.url`, not `shape.meta`.** `meta` needs no migration (it's `T.jsonValue`), but it would require hand-rolling the menu item and dialog — exactly the "separate text-shape implementation" the ticket forbids.
- **A migration is mandatory, not optional.** `T.linkUrl.optional()` doesn't work: the gate is `'url' in props`, which is false when the key is absent, so old text shapes would silently never show **Edit link**. Without the migration, `migrateStoreSnapshot` reports *success* and does nothing, then validation throws `At shape(type = text).props.url: Expected string, got undefined`.
- **Backfill defensively** (`if (props.url === undefined)`). An earlier Roam migration assigned unconditionally and clobbered user values (PR #916).
- **Replace, don't append, the default text util.** Registering both `TextShapeUtil` and a subclass throws *"defined more than once"*.
- **Vendor the hyperlink button.** tldraw does not export `HyperlinkButton` (confirmed absent from `dist-esm/index.d.mts`); mirror its markup and reuse the stock `.tl-hyperlink-button` CSS already vendored at `src/styles/style.css:1036`.

## Obsidian-specific deltas

| | Roam | Obsidian |
|---|---|---|
| Registration sites | 4 | **2** — `utils/tldraw.ts:55` and `TldrawViewComponent.tsx:109` |
| Migration home | appended v6 to `com.roam-research.discourse-graphs` | **new sequence at v1** (see below) |
| Sync worker | needed `"text"` added to `shapeType` params | **N/A** — file-based; cross-tab merge goes through `store.schema.migrateStoreSnapshot`, which applies the retroactive migration |
| Test infra | vitest exists | **none — must be stood up** |

The migration goes in a **new** sequence `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link` starting at version 1, not appended to `discourseNodeMigrations`. Roam appended because its sequence is generically named; Obsidian's existing one is `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.discourse-node`, and a text-shape migration doesn't belong there. `createMigrationSequence` only rejects sequences that don't *start* at 1, so a fresh sequence is legal. `retroactive` defaults to `true`, which is what makes it backfill files that predate it.

## Implementation

### 1. `src/components/canvas/shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` (new)

Port of `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`:

```tsx
const textShapeWithLinkProps = { ...textShapeProps, url: T.linkUrl };

export class TextShapeWithLinkUtil extends TextShapeUtil {
  static override props = textShapeWithLinkProps;

  override getDefaultProps(): TextShapeWithLinkProps {
    return { ...super.getDefaultProps(), url: "" };
  }

  override component(shape: TLTextShape): ReturnType<TextShapeUtil["component"]> {
    const url = getTextShapeUrl(shape);
    return (<>{super.component(shape)}{url && <HyperlinkButton url={url} .../>}</>) as ...;
  }
}
```

Three things that are load-bearing:
- **`getDefaultProps` must be overridden.** `static props` alone does not add a default — the base returns an object literal, so every `createShape({type:"text"})` would fail validation on `props.url`.
- **`super.component(shape)`** rather than reimplementing the label: `useTextShapeKeydownHandler` is module-private, so a rewrite would silently drop Cmd+Enter-to-complete.
- Statics are inherited, so `static migrations = textShapeMigrations` stays untouched and keeps sequence id `com.tldraw.shape.text`. `processPropsMigrations` asserts that id for any sequence attached to the util — which is *why* the url backfill has to be a separate store-level sequence.

Roam's version reads `this.editor.getZoomLevel()` at render time rather than through `useValue`; mirror it for consistency (the hide-when-zoomed-out threshold is cosmetic).

### 2. `src/components/canvas/utils/textShapeLink.ts` (new)

Pure, dependency-free helpers, ported verbatim from `apps/roam/src/utils/textShapeLink.ts`: `isTextShapeRecord`, `hasLinkUrlProp`, `backfillTextShapeUrl`. These exist so the migration logic is unit-testable without an editor or the Obsidian API.

### 3. `src/components/canvas/shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts` (new)

Mirrors `discourseNodeMigrations.ts:36-53`: `createMigrationSequence({ sequenceId: "com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link", sequence: [{ id: versions.AddTextShapeUrl /* 1 */, scope: "record", filter: isTextShapeRecord, up: backfillTextShapeUrl, down: (s) => delete s.props.url }] })`.

### 4. `src/components/canvas/shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts` (new) + both registration sites

```ts
export const baseShapeUtils: TLAnyShapeUtilConstructor[] =
  defaultShapeUtils.map((util) => (util === TextShapeUtil ? TextShapeWithLinkUtil : util));
```

Then `...defaultShapeUtils` → `...baseShapeUtils` at **`utils/tldraw.ts:56`** and **`TldrawViewComponent.tsx:109`**, and register the migration at `utils/tldraw.ts:68` (`migrations: [discourseNodeMigrations, textLinkMigrations]`).

These two lists are consumed independently — `createTLStore` uses one for the *schema*, the `Editor` uses the other for *rendering* — and **nothing asserts they agree**. Update only the component and `updateShapes` throws on validation; update only the store and links persist but never render. That silent divergence is the reason for the shared module, same as Roam's `baseShapeUtils.ts`.

`createRawTldrawFile`'s bare `createTLStore()` at `utils/tldraw.ts:92` is left alone — it only runs with zero records, and retroactive migrations backfill on load regardless.

### 5. Test infrastructure (new for this workspace)

`apps/obsidian` has no tests at all. Mirror `apps/roam/vitest.config.mts`:

- `apps/obsidian/vitest.config.mts` — `environment: "node"`, `include: ["src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts"]`, `resolve.alias` for `~` → `src` (tsconfig paths aren't honoured automatically).
- `apps/obsidian/package.json` — add `"test": "pnpm test:unit"`, `"test:unit": "vitest run --config vitest.config.mts"`, and `"vitest": "catalog:"` to devDependencies. Per [memory: avoid `pnpm add` here], edit `package.json` by hand and run plain `pnpm install`.
- No turbo.json change: `turbo.json:78-80` already defines a generic `test:unit`, and root `ci:validate` picks it up.
- No `obsidian` module stub needed — the test imports only `tldraw` and the pure helpers. (`tldraw` imports fine headless in plain node; no jsdom.)
- `vitest` must be a real devDep because `tsconfig.json`'s `include: ["**/*.ts"]` puts the test files under `check-types`.

`src/components/canvas/utils/__tests__/textShapeLink.test.ts` ports Roam's suite: the backfill is idempotent and never overwrites a user value, non-text records are untouched, a migrated shape satisfies the `'url' in props` gate an unmigrated one fails, and — via `createTLSchema` with an extended text schema — an unmigrated text shape **throws on validation** while a migrated one round-trips its url through `migrateStoreSnapshot`. That last pair is the highest-value test: the real failure mode is `TldrawView.tsx:126-129` swallowing the throw and rendering a blank canvas.

## Known tradeoffs to surface in the PR

- **`obsidian://` page links will not work.** `T.linkUrl` accepts only `http:`/`https:`/`mailto:` (`@tldraw/validate` `validLinkProtocols`), and tldraw's `EditLinkDialog` rejects other protocols on input before the schema ever sees them. So "link to a page" — which the ticket calls the primary expected target — isn't reachable through this path. This *is* exact geo parity and matches "no new link format"; Roam shipped the same. Flag it and suggest a follow-up ticket rather than forking the dialog.
- **Forward incompatibility:** a canvas saved with a text url, opened by an *older* plugin build, fails validation and renders blank. No data loss — `onLoadFile` returns early, so the autosave listener never attaches and the file isn't overwritten. `discourseNodeMigrations` set this precedent; worth a release note.
- **Convert To drops the url.** `convertToDiscourseNode.ts` only reads `props.richText`. Correct (text→node conversion is out of scope), but say so in the PR so it isn't read as a regression.
- Worth a Linear comment to Michael that "reuse the geo-shape link code path" rested on a wrong premise, so the change isn't read as ignoring the instruction. Same note applies to ENG-2227.

## Verification

**Static** — `pnpm --filter @discourse-graphs/obsidian check-types`, `lint`, `test:unit`, `build`. Then grep `dist/main.js` for `AddTextShapeUrl` and `tl-hyperlink-button` to confirm the build actually contains the change. Lint: check for new *warnings* on added lines, not just errors — CI's `lint-changed-files` fails on warnings while local lint exits 0.

**In Obsidian** (the part static checks can't cover — ENG-2227 is still blocked on exactly this):
1. Text shape → right-click → Edit ▸ **Edit link** is present. Select two shapes, or lock the shape → absent.
2. Set `https://example.com` → corner icon appears; click → opens; reopen dialog → pre-filled; **Clear** → icon gone.
3. **The icon's stacking is the most likely thing to be wrong.** `.tl-text-wrapper .tl-text-content` is `pointer-events: all; z-index: var(--layer-text-content)` (`style.css:806-809`) while the button is `z-index: 1` — so for a text shape the label may cover the icon and swallow the click, in a way it doesn't for geo. Check unselected / selected / editing. If it misbehaves, the fix is one CSS rule raising the button to `--layer-text-content` (tree order then favours the later sibling, and the `--layer-text-editor` overlay still wins while editing) — **not** a wrapper div. Don't add the rule pre-emptively.
4. Double-click-to-edit still works outside the 44×44 corner.
5. **Persistence** (explicit Done When): close and reopen the canvas; then read the raw `tldraw-data` block and confirm `url` is on the text record and `schema.sequences` contains `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link: 1`.
6. **Backfill:** open a canvas file created *before* this change containing a text shape — it must load (not blank) and accept a link.
7. **Cross-tab:** same canvas in two panes; add a link in one, confirm it merges (`canvasFileSync.ts`).

Before trusting any in-app run: another worktree's dev watcher shares `~/Documents/testVault/.obsidian/plugins/discourse-graphs`, so grep the built bundle for `AddTextShapeUrl` to confirm the vault has *this* worktree's build.

## Files

**New** — `src/components/canvas/shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts`, `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts`, `utils/textShapeLink.ts`, `utils/__tests__/textShapeLink.test.ts`, `apps/obsidian/vitest.config.mts` (all under `apps/obsidian/`).

**Modified** — `src/components/canvas/utils/tldraw.ts` (lines 56, 68), `src/components/canvas/TldrawViewComponent.tsx` (line 109), `apps/obsidian/package.json`.

**Reference** — the ENG-2227 worktree at `.claude/worktrees/eng-2227-add-link-support-to-tldraw-text-shapes-in-roam` (uncommitted; `git diff HEAD` shows the full Roam implementation).

## Implementation

### 1. `src/components/canvas/shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` (new)

Port of `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`:

```tsx
const textShapeWithLinkProps = { ...textShapeProps, url: T.linkUrl };

export class TextShapeWithLinkUtil extends TextShapeUtil {
  static override props = textShapeWithLinkProps;

  override getDefaultProps(): TextShapeWithLinkProps {
    return { ...super.getDefaultProps(), url: "" };
  }

  override component(shape: TLTextShape): ReturnType<TextShapeUtil["component"]> {
    const url = getTextShapeUrl(shape);
    return (<>{super.component(shape)}{url && <HyperlinkButton url={url} .../>}</>) as ...;

```


No — the defensive backfill and the optional-vs-required choice are independent. Verified in `@tldraw/validate@3.14.2`:

**What `optional()` changes.** `ObjectValidator` calls `validator.validate(getOwnProperty(obj, key))`, so a missing key arrives as `undefined`, and `optional()` returns early on `undefined` (`validation.mjs:594-598`). So yes — with `T.linkUrl.optional()` an un-backfilled text shape *validates* instead of throwing `Expected string, got undefined`.

**What it doesn't change.** The defensive `if (props.url === undefined)` guards a different failure: a migration `up` running over a record that *already* has a url and clobbering it with `""`. That's what bit Roam in PR #916. Optionality has no bearing on it — you'd keep the check either way. It's one line.

**And it doesn't remove the migration.** The eligibility gate is `'url' in props`, which is false when the key is absent. Optional-without-migration means every pre-existing text shape silently never shows **Edit link** while new ones do. So the migration is still mandatory; optional only changes what happens *if the migration doesn't run*.

So the real question is what you want that miss to look like:

- **Required** → loud: validation throws, `TldrawView.createStore` swallows it (`TldrawView.tsx:126-129`), canvas renders blank.
- **Optional** → silent: canvas opens, link UI just never appears on old shapes.

I'd keep it **required**, for three reasons. The upgrade path is already covered — the retroactive sequence runs on every load path including the cross-tab merge. The downgrade path isn't helped at all: a new file opened by an older build throws `Unexpected property` on `url` because the *old* build's validator config has no such key, regardless of how we declare it. And geo itself is `url: T.linkUrl` required, so required is literal parity — which is the ticket's framing and what ENG-2227 shipped.

What optional actually buys is turning "our migration is buggy" from a loud failure into a quiet one, and I'd rather that be loud in dev than invisible in users' vaults.

One correction to my plan either way: I wrote that `T.linkUrl.optional()` "doesn't work," which is too strong — it validates fine, it just doesn't let you skip the migration. I'll fix that line.

Here's what actually blocks page links, and what each layer costs to change.

**Three layers say no today, not one:**

1. **The validator.** `T.linkUrl` accepts only `http:`/`https:`/`mailto:` (`validation.mjs:642`). `obsidian://open?...` is rejected by the schema.
2. **The dialog.** `EditLinkDialog.validateUrl` gates on `T.linkUrl.isValid` and otherwise retries with `https://` prepended (`EditLinkDialog.tsx:17-25`). It rejects non-web protocols *before* the schema ever sees them, so widening the validator alone changes nothing.
3. **The affordance.** `<a href target="_blank">` — fine for the web, wrong for opening a vault page in a leaf.

**What I'd been missing: this plugin already has a page-reference format, and it's better than `obsidian://`.** Discourse node shapes don't store a URL. `assetStore.ts:39-50` appends a real block to the canvas markdown —

```
[[Some Page]]
^<uuid>
```

— and stores `props.src = "asset:obsidian.blockref.<uuid>"`. `resolveLinkedTFileByBlockRef` (`assetStore.ts:77`) reads it back via `metadataCache.getFirstLinkpathDest`. Because the link is a genuine wikilink in the file, Obsidian's own machinery sees it: backlinks, graph view, and rename-following all work. An `obsidian://` string buried in our fenced JSON block gets none of that and breaks when the vault or page is renamed.

So the three real options:

| | Work | Page links |
|---|---|---|
| **Geo parity** (planned) | as planned | none |
| **`obsidian://` URLs** | widen validator + fork dialog | fragile: no backlinks, breaks on rename |
| **Block-ref wikilinks** | + action override, page picker, click branch | first-class |

The third is the one worth doing, and most of its parts exist: `overrides.actions` is a supported extension point (`TLUiOverrides.actions`, `index.d.mts:3747`), so we'd swap only `edit-link`'s `onSelect` to open our dialog while the menu item, label, icon, placement and eligibility gate stay stock; `SuggestInput.tsx`/`PublishGroupSuggestModal.tsx` give the picker; `openFileInSidebar` gives the click. We're already vendoring the button, so branching web-vs-page there is free.

Two things you should weigh before picking it. It goes past three of the ticket's explicit out-of-scope lines — page picker, new link format, and "reuse the geo-shape link code path" — so it's a re-scope, not a judgment call I should make quietly. And ENG-2227 shipped Roam as web-URL-only, so choosing this for Obsidian diverges the two apps until Roam gets an equivalent.

# ENG-2228 — Add link support to tldraw text shapes in Obsidian

## Context

Text shapes on the Obsidian tldraw canvas can't carry a link, so a simplified canvas narrative can't open the detailed source its text stands for. Geo shapes can.

**The ticket's "reuse the geo-shape link code path" premise is wrong**, as ENG-2227 already established on the Roam side. There is no app-side geo-link code in `apps/obsidian` — the **Edit link** action, `EditLinkDialog` and the corner icon are all stock tldraw 3.14.2. Eligibility is duck-typed, not an allowlist:

```ts
// node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts:173 — useHasLinkShapeSelected
!!(shape && shape.type !== 'embed' && 'url' in shape.props && !shape.isLocked)
```

`TLGeoShape` declares `url`; `TLTextShape` does not. So the core of this is a **schema change**: once `text` props carry `url`, the menu item appears for free (`CustomContextMenu.tsx:65` renders `<DefaultContextMenuContent />`, and no `actions` override exists today).

## Approved Plan:
# ENG-2228 — Add link support to tldraw text shapes in Obsidian

## Context

Text shapes on the Obsidian tldraw canvas can't carry a link, so a simplified canvas narrative can't open the detailed source its text stands for. Geo shapes can.

**The ticket's "reuse the geo-shape link code path" premise is wrong**, as ENG-2227 already established on the Roam side. There is no app-side geo-link code in `apps/obsidian` — the **Edit link** action, `EditLinkDialog` and the corner icon are all stock tldraw 3.14.2. Eligibility is duck-typed, not an allowlist:

```ts
// node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/hooks/menu-hooks.ts:173 — useHasLinkShapeSelected
!!(shape && shape.type !== 'embed' && 'url' in shape.props && !shape.isLocked)
```

`TLGeoShape` declares `url`; `TLTextShape` does not. So the core of this is a **schema change**: once `text` props carry `url`, the menu item appears for free (`CustomContextMenu.tsx:65` renders `<DefaultContextMenuContent />`, and no `actions` override exists today).

**Scope decision (2026-09-14):** the ticket names page links as the primary target, so this ships `obsidian://open?vault=…&file=…` support alongside web URLs. That goes beyond strict geo parity and beyond what ENG-2227 shipped for Roam — deliberately. `obsidian://` is already this canvas's link currency: `parseObsidianOpenUrl` (`externalContentHandlers.ts:33`) and `buildObsidianUrl` (`wikilinkDragHandler.ts:14`) exist, and dropping such a URL on the canvas already creates a discourse node shape.

*Known limitation to state in the PR:* an `obsidian://` URL inside our fenced JSON block is invisible to Obsidian's link machinery — no backlinks, no graph view, and it breaks if the vault or page is renamed. The plugin's own richer pattern for this (a real `[[wikilink]]` block plus a block-ref id in `props.src`, `assetStore.ts:39-50`) survives renames. Worth a follow-up ticket; not this one.

## Decisions inherited from ENG-2227

- **Store the link in `shape.props.url`, not `shape.meta`.** `meta` needs no migration but would require hand-rolling the menu item.
- **A migration is mandatory.** `T.linkUrl.optional()` *does* validate an absent key (`optional()` returns early on `undefined`, `validation.mjs:594-598`) — but the gate is `'url' in props`, which is false when the key is missing, so pre-existing text shapes would silently never show **Edit link**. Optional only changes what a migration *miss* looks like.
- **`url` is required, not optional** (confirmed 2026-09-14): geo parity, and a migration miss then fails loudly rather than silently hiding the feature. Optional wouldn't help the downgrade case anyway — an older build throws `Unexpected property` on `url` regardless, since its own validator config has no such key.
- **Backfill defensively** (`if (props.url === undefined)`) — independent of the required/optional choice. An earlier Roam migration assigned unconditionally and clobbered user values (PR #916).
- **Replace, don't append, the default text util.** Registering both throws *"defined more than once"*.
- **Vendor the hyperlink button.** tldraw does not export `HyperlinkButton` (absent from `dist-esm/index.d.mts`); mirror its markup and reuse the stock `.tl-hyperlink-button` CSS already vendored at `src/styles/style.css:1036`.

## Implementation

### 1. `shapes/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` (new)

Port of `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, with the validator and click handling widened:

```tsx
static override props = { ...textShapeProps, url: textLinkUrl };
override getDefaultProps() { return { ...super.getDefaultProps(), url: "" }; }
override component(shape) { return <>{super.component(shape)}{url && <HyperlinkButton .../>}</>; }
```

Load-bearing details:
- **`getDefaultProps` must be overridden.** `static props` alone gives no default — the base returns an object literal, so `createShape({type:"text"})` would fail validation on `props.url`.
- **Call `super.component(shape)`** rather than reimplementing the label: `useTextShapeKeydownHandler` is module-private, so a rewrite silently drops Cmd+Enter-to-complete.
- Statics are inherited, so `static migrations = textShapeMigrations` stays untouched at sequence id `com.tldraw.shape.text`. `processPropsMigrations` asserts that id for any sequence attached to the util — which is *why* the url backfill must be a separate store-level sequence.
- Roam's version reads `this.editor.getZoomLevel()` at render time rather than via `useValue`; mirror it (the hide-when-zoomed-out threshold is cosmetic).

### 2. `utils/textShapeLink.ts` (new)

Pure, dependency-free helpers ported from `apps/roam/src/utils/textShapeLink.ts` (`isTextShapeRecord`, `hasLinkUrlProp`, `backfillTextShapeUrl`), plus the widened validator:

```ts
const ALLOWED_PROTOCOLS = ["http:", "https:", "mailto:", "obsidian:"];
export const textLinkUrl = T.string.check(validateTextLinkUrl);
```

**This allowlist is a security boundary, not a formality** — the affordance renders `<a href={url}>`, so accepting arbitrary protocols would make `javascript:` an XSS vector. Enumerate; never fall through to "anything that parses".

Keeping these helpers free of `obsidian` imports is what makes them unit-testable without mocks.

### 3. `shapes/textLinkMigrations.ts` (new)

Mirrors `discourseNodeMigrations.ts:36-53`: `createMigrationSequence({ sequenceId: "com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link", sequence: [{ id: versions.AddTextShapeUrl /* 1 */, scope: "record", filter: isTextShapeRecord, up: backfillTextShapeUrl, down: (s) => delete s.props.url }] })`.

A **new** sequence starting at v1, not appended to `discourseNodeMigrations` — Roam appended because its sequence is generically named, whereas Obsidian's is `…obsidian.discourse-node` and a text migration doesn't belong there. `createMigrationSequence` only rejects sequences that don't *start* at 1. `retroactive` defaults to `true`, which is what backfills files predating it.

### 4. `shapes/baseShapeUtils.ts` (new) + both registration sites

```ts
export const baseShapeUtils = defaultShapeUtils.map((u) =>
  u === TextShapeUtil ? TextShapeWithLinkUtil : u);
```

Swap `...defaultShapeUtils` → `...baseShapeUtils` at **`utils/tldraw.ts:56`** and **`TldrawViewComponent.tsx:109`**, and register the migration at `utils/tldraw.ts:68`.

These two lists are consumed independently — `createTLStore` for the *schema*, the `Editor` for *rendering* — and **nothing asserts they agree**. Update only the component and `updateShapes` throws; update only the store and links persist but never render. Hence the shared module, as in Roam's `baseShapeUtils.ts`.

`createRawTldrawFile`'s bare `createTLStore()` at `utils/tldraw.ts:92` is left alone — zero records, and retroactive migrations backfill on load anyway.

### 5. `TextLinkDialog.tsx` (new) + an `edit-link` action override

tldraw's dialog gates on `T.linkUrl.isValid` and retries with `https://` prepended (`EditLinkDialog.tsx:17-25`), so it rejects `obsidian://` *before* the schema sees it. Widening the validator alone accomplishes nothing — the dialog must be forked.

`EditLinkDialog` itself is not exported, but every primitive it uses is (`TldrawUiDialogBody/Header/Footer/Title/CloseButton`, `TldrawUiInput`, `TldrawUiButton`, `TldrawUiButtonLabel`), so the fork is a faithful, visually identical copy with `validateUrl` swapped.

Swap it in via the supported `TLUiOverrides.actions` hook (`index.d.mts:3747`), extending the existing `overrides` object at `TldrawViewComponent.tsx:466` (currently `tools` only). Replace only `edit-link`'s `onSelect` — `helpers.addDialog({ component: TextLinkDialog })`, preceded by `editor.markHistoryStoppingPoint("edit-link")` as the stock action does (`actions.tsx:153-160`). Label, icon, placement and the eligibility gate all stay stock.

**The trap:** this override is global, so the forked dialog also serves *geo* shapes — whose `url` prop is still stock `T.linkUrl`. Letting an `obsidian://` URL through for a geo shape would throw at `editor.updateShapes`. The dialog must therefore pick its validator from the selected shape's type (wide for `text`, stock `T.linkUrl` otherwise). Cover this with a test; it is the most likely silent regression in the change.

### 6. Click handling in the vendored button

Branch on protocol. Web/mailto → plain `<a href target="_blank">`, exactly as geo. `obsidian:` → `preventDefault`, then `parseObsidianOpenUrl` (`externalContentHandlers.ts:33`) → resolve to a `TFile` → `openFileInSidebar` (`openFileUtils.ts:68`). Handling it in-app avoids an OS protocol round trip that would defocus and re-enter Obsidian.

`resolveObsidianUrlToFile` (`externalContentHandlers.ts:56`) already does the vault-name check and the `.md` suffix retry — export it rather than writing a second copy. Show a `Notice` when the target is another vault or missing (per house style, `Notice`, not `console.*`).

### 7. Test infrastructure (new for this workspace)

`apps/obsidian` has no tests at all. Mirror `apps/roam/vitest.config.mts`:

- `apps/obsidian/vitest.config.mts` — `environment: "node"`, `include: ["src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts"]`, `resolve.alias` `~` → `src` (tsconfig paths aren't honoured automatically).
- `apps/obsidian/package.json` — add `"test": "pnpm test:unit"`, `"test:unit": "vitest run --config vitest.config.mts"`, and `"vitest": "catalog:"`. Per [memory] edit `package.json` by hand and run plain `pnpm install`, not `pnpm add`, to keep the lockfile diff small.
- No `turbo.json` change — `turbo.json:78-80` already defines a generic `test:unit`, which root `ci:validate` picks up.
- `vitest` must be a real devDep: `tsconfig.json`'s `include: ["**/*.ts"]` puts test files under `check-types`.
- No `obsidian` module stub needed if tests import only `tldraw` and the pure helpers. (`tldraw` imports fine headless; no jsdom.)

`utils/__tests__/textShapeLink.test.ts` ports Roam's suite plus the new validator cases:
- backfill is idempotent, never overwrites a user value, leaves non-text records alone;
- a migrated shape satisfies the `'url' in props` gate an unmigrated one fails;
- via `createTLSchema` with an extended text schema, an unmigrated text shape **throws on validation** while a migrated one round-trips its url through `migrateStoreSnapshot` — the highest-value test, since the real failure mode is `TldrawView.tsx:126-129` swallowing the throw into a blank canvas;
- `textLinkUrl` accepts http/https/mailto/`obsidian://open?…` and **rejects `javascript:`**, `file:`, and unparseable junk;
- the dialog picks the wide validator for `text` and the stock one for `geo`.

## Verification

**Static** — `pnpm --filter @discourse-graphs/obsidian check-types`, `lint`, `test:unit`, `build`; then grep `dist/main.js` for `AddTextShapeUrl` and `tl-hyperlink-button` to confirm the build contains the change. Check for new lint *warnings* on added lines, not just errors — CI's `lint-changed-files` fails on warnings while local lint exits 0.

**In Obsidian:**
1. Text shape → right-click → Edit ▸ **Edit link** present. Two shapes selected, or shape locked → absent.
2. `https://example.com` → icon appears; click opens; reopening the dialog pre-fills; **Clear** removes it.
3. **Page link:** copy a page's Obsidian URL, paste it in, confirm the dialog *accepts* it (this is what the fork exists for) and clicking opens that page in the sidebar without the window defocusing.
4. **Geo regression:** a geo shape still takes a web URL, and an `obsidian://` URL on a geo shape is rejected by the dialog rather than throwing.
5. **Icon stacking is the likeliest visual bug.** `.tl-text-wrapper .tl-text-content` is `pointer-events: all; z-index: var(--layer-text-content)` (`style.css:806-809`) while the button is `z-index: 1`, so a text shape's label may cover the icon and swallow the click in a way it doesn't for geo. Check unselected / selected / editing. If it misbehaves, the fix is one CSS rule raising the button to `--layer-text-content` (tree order then favours the later sibling, and `--layer-text-editor` still wins while editing) — **not** a wrapper div. Don't add it pre-emptively.
6. Double-click-to-edit still works outside the 44×44 corner.
7. **Persistence** (explicit Done When): close and reopen the canvas; read the raw `tldraw-data` block and confirm `url` is on the text record and `schema.sequences` contains `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link: 1`.
8. **Backfill:** open a canvas created *before* this change containing a text shape — it must load (not blank) and accept a link.
9. **Cross-tab:** same canvas in two panes; add a link in one, confirm it merges (`canvasFileSync.ts`).

Before trusting any in-app run: another worktree's dev watcher shares `~/Documents/testVault/.obsidian/plugins/discourse-graphs`, so grep the built bundle for `AddTextShapeUrl` to confirm the vault has *this* worktree's build.

## PR notes

- Say that "reuse the geo-shape link code path" rested on a wrong premise (no such app-side code exists) so the change isn't read as ignoring the instruction — same note applies to ENG-2227. Worth a Linear comment to Michael.
- Flag the divergence from ENG-2227: Obsidian accepts `obsidian://`, Roam is web-only.
- Flag the rename/backlink limitation of `obsidian://` and propose the block-ref follow-up.
- **Forward incompatibility:** a canvas saved with a text url, opened by an *older* plugin build, fails validation and renders blank. No data loss — `onLoadFile` returns early so the autosave listener never attaches and the file isn't overwritten. `discourseNodeMigrations` set this precedent; worth a release note.
- **Convert To drops the url** (`convertToDiscourseNode.ts` reads only `props.richText`). Correct, since text→node conversion is out of scope, but say so explicitly.

Obsidian is Electron, so it can be driven over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Relaunch with
`open -na /Applications/Obsidian.app --args --remote-debugging-port=9222`, then attach over
`ws` to the target from `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/list`. Verified working August 2026 on
Obsidian 1.8.4 / macOS — 23/23 assertions driving the ENG-2113 search footer.

Key points learned the hard way:

- **Attach to an already-open vault** instead of rewriting `~/Library/Application Support/obsidian/obsidian.json`
  to select one. The rewrite is how PR #959 selects a vault and it is also that PR's worst bug —
  if launch throws afterwards, teardown never runs and the user's global Obsidian config stays clobbered.
- Several CDP page targets exist (devtools, popouts, one per vault). Pick by
  `document.querySelector(".workspace")` **and** `app.vault.getName() === "<vault>"` — title matching alone
  is not enough when multiple vaults are open.
- Reload the plugin between runs so fresh code is tested:
  `app.plugins.disablePlugin(id).then(() => app.plugins.enablePlugin(id))`. Plugin id is
  `@discourse-graph/obsidian`, so command ids look like `@discourse-graph/obsidian:open-node-search`.
- `Runtime.evaluate` bodies are wrapped in a plain function, so `await` at the top level throws —
  return a promise chain instead.
- Playwright is **not** required; ~40 lines of raw CDP over `ws` covers evaluate, `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`,
  `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, and `Page.captureScreenshot`.
- To distinguish "new tab" from "split", compare a root-leaf count against
  `app.workspace.rootSplit.children.length` — a new tab raises leaves only, a split raises both.
  **`iterateRootLeaves` stops early when the callback returns a truthy value**, so
  `iterateRootLeaves(() => n++)` silently caps the count at 2 (post-increment returns 1 on the
  second call). Use a block body: `iterateRootLeaves(() => { n++; })`.
- **Poll conditions, never sleep.** A 10-line `waitFor(expr)` that evaluates every 25ms took one
  scenario from 24.3s to 1.2s — 8.8s of that was literal `sleep()` calls, and only 0.35s of real
  waiting was ever needed. Naive fixed-sleep CDP is slower than Playwright; polled CDP is a wash.
- Reset workspace state at the start of a scenario, or assertions inherit leftover tabs and splits.
  `getLeaf("tab")` **reuses an empty active leaf** rather than adding one, so with a dirty workspace
  a correct new-tab implementation reads as a failure.
- Close a stray modal with an Escape key event rather than a programmatic `body.click()` — a
  synthetic click on `body` does not hit the modal's background element, so it will not dismiss it.
- **The developer is using the app while the harness drives it.** A human opening tabs or modals
  mid-run perturbs state and produces failures that look like code bugs. Re-run before believing a
  causal story built on one observation: this session produced a confident, wrong diagnosis
  ("`detachLeavesOfType` + `openFile` in one `evaluate` loses the file") that failed to reproduce
  3/3 times once tested deliberately. The real cause was concurrent human interaction. A baseline
  reset at scenario start makes runs robust to this; a dedicated vault would isolate it properly.
- **The Obsidian window must be visible (`document.visibilityState === "visible"`) while scenarios
  run.** When it is covered/minimised/on another Space, Chromium throttles the renderer's timers —
  100 ms → 300–900 ms, and after ~5 min hidden to once per minute — so anything built on
  `setTimeout` (a 500 ms save debounce, a sync debounce, a poll loop *inside* the page) silently
  stalls. It presents as "the feature is broken" (writes land minutes later) with zero errors.
  ENG-2107 lost an hour to this. Check `visibilityState` and a 100 ms timer's real latency before
  believing a timing failure; `electronWindow.setAlwaysOnTop(true)` helps only until focus changes,
  so ask the user to click the window and poll `visibilityState` before firing the scenario.
- The auto-mode classifier blocks quit-and-relaunch as one compound Bash command; run the steps separately.
- **`editor.hasFocus()` is not measurable from CDP.** It reads `false` even for a plain
  `editor.focus()` with no modal involved and `document.hasFocus() === true`; no element holds DOM
  focus at all (`document.activeElement` is the top-level app div). Take a **baseline** measurement
  of the same assertion outside the feature under test before believing a focus failure — ENG-2114
  looked like a focus regression until the baseline failed identically. Assert the observable
  consequence instead (cursor position advanced past the inserted text).
- **Stale `.modal-container` elements poison selectors.** A scenario that times out or throws leaves
  its modal in the DOM, so the next run's `querySelector(".modal-container .modal")` reads the *old*
  modal — producing "footer missing the action" and "modal did not close" failures while the feature
  actually works. Start every scenario with
  `document.querySelectorAll(".modal-container").forEach(el => el.remove())`.
- The plugin **folder** is `discourse-graphs` but the **id** is `@discourse-graph/obsidian`; passing the
  folder name to `disablePlugin`/`enablePlugin` silently no-ops (`loaded: false`, `manifests[folder]`
  undefined). Read the real id from `app.plugins.manifests`, whose `dir` field maps id → folder.

A fuller Playwright + CDP harness already exists on branch
`worktree-eng-1583-automate-obsidian-dev-environment-load-and-visual-validation` (PR #959, ENG-1583):
launch, vault switching, command palette driving, modal helpers, step screenshots. It is open with
CHANGES_REQUESTED — the blocking objection is documentation quality, not the mechanism — and is far
behind main. Reuse its `e2e/helpers/obsidian-setup.ts` rather than rediscovering the launch tricks.

Unrelated dev-loop gotcha hit while doing this: editing only a file under `apps/obsidian/src/styles/`
never triggers a rebuild, because the concatenation runs in esbuild's `onEnd` while those files sit
outside its module graph. Touch a `.ts` file to force it. See [[feedback-obsidian-no-console]] for the
related Notice-instead-of-console rule in this app.

input.content:
---
name: reference-tldraw-store-put-no-listener
description: "tldraw store.listen() does not fire for a programmatic store.put(), so CDP-driven canvas edits never trigger the autosave — drive real input events instead"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

A raw `store.put()` on the Obsidian canvas's `TLStore` (reachable over CDP as
`app.workspace.getLeavesOfType("tldraw-dg-preview")[0].view.store`) updates the store and
re-renders the shape, but **fires no `store.listen()` callbacks** — verified by registering a
listener with the same `{ source: "user", scope: "document" }` options the plugin uses and
counting 0 calls. The plugin's autosave hangs off that listener, so programmatic puts never
reach the markdown file and look like a persistence bug in whatever you just built.

Diagnose it by checking the *store* and the *file* separately over time: shape present in
store + absent from file, indefinitely, means the listener never fired — not that saving is broken.

Drive real input instead (`Input.dispatchMouseEvent` / `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` /
`Input.insertText`): select the tool, click to place, type, Escape. That exercises the editor,
flushes the reactor, and the 500 ms `DEFAULT_SAVE_DELAY` debounce then writes the file. Real
input is also the only way to test shape *creation*, which is where `getDefaultProps` bugs
surface.

Related gotchas found the same way:
- `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` rejects `text: undefined` — omit the key entirely on `keyUp` and for
  non-printable keys like Escape, or CDP returns `Invalid 'text' parameter`.
- Counting `.tl-shape` elements immediately after a store load reads 0 because React has not
  painted yet. Poll for the count instead of asserting once, or you will misread viewport
  culling / paint timing as a blank canvas.
- `document.elementFromPoint` at a shape's hyperlink icon returns `.tl-canvas`, not the anchor —
  for geo shapes too. tldraw hit-tests through its own canvas layer, so this is not evidence of a
  z-index bug. Always measure a stock shape type as a control before believing a rendering regression.

See [[reference-obsidian-cdp-driving]] for attaching to a vault over CDP.

content.text:
ENG-2228 is implemented and verified end-to-end. Changes are uncommitted on `eng-2228-add-link-support-to-tldraw-text-shapes-in-obsidian`.

## What it does

Text shapes gained a `url` prop, which is all tldraw's duck-typed gate (`'url' in shape.props`) needs — the **Edit link** item, its icon and placement come from stock tldraw untouched. Because you chose page-link support, the validator is widened past tldraw's `T.linkUrl` to an explicit allowlist (`http`/`https`/`mailto`/`obsidian`), and the dialog is forked, since tldraw's own rejects non-web protocols on input before the schema ever sees them.

**New:** `TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx`, `baseShapeUtils.ts`, `textLinkMigrations.ts`, `utils/textShapeLink.ts`, `TextLinkDialog.tsx`, tests, `vitest.config.mts`.
**Modified:** the two shape-util registration sites, the `overrides` block, `externalContentHandlers.ts` (export the resolver), `styles.css`, `package.json`.

## Verified in Obsidian, not just statically

`ci:validate` green (6 tasks, 0 cached); types, lint, build clean; 10 new unit tests. Then driven over CDP against testVault:

- **Edit link** appears under Edit ▸ for a text shape
- The forked dialog accepts an `obsidian://` URL and enables Save — stock tldraw would have blocked it
- Clicking the icon opens the target page in the sidebar
- A text shape created through the real toolbar gets `url: ""` — without the `getDefaultProps` override every text-shape creation would have thrown
- A link survived a full close/reopen through the markdown, and `com.discourse-graph.obsidian.text-link: 1` is recorded in the file
- A genuine pre-change file (url stripped, sequence removed) loads, backfills both text shapes to `url: ""`, and renders — no blank canvas
- `javascript:` is rejected by the allowlist, which matters because the affordance is an `<a href>`

Two things I flagged in the plan turned out not to be real. The z-index concern didn't materialize — a geo shape measures **identically**, so that's tldraw's hit-testing, not a text-specific regression. And an early "nothing persists" result was my harness, not the code: tldraw's `store.listen` doesn't fire for a programmatic `store.put`, so autosave never ran; real input events save fine. I've saved that one to memory.

## Worth knowing before the PR

- **`obsidian://` links are invisible to Obsidian's link graph** — no backlinks, and they break on vault or page rename. The plugin's own `[[wikilink]]` + block-ref pattern (`assetStore.ts:39-50`) survives renames. I'd open a follow-up.
- This **diverges from ENG-2227**, which shipped Roam web-URL-only.
- The ticket's "reuse the geo-shape link code path" premise is wrong — there is no such app-side code. Worth a Linear comment to Michael so the change isn't read as ignoring it.

Two cleanups pending your call: I deleted the test canvases I created, but **Obsidian is still running with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`** — want me to relaunch it normally? And shall I commit and open the PR?

**Result:** A text shape can carry a link with the same **Edit link** action and corner affordance as a geo shape, and the link survives closing and reopening the canvas. The link may be a web/mailto URL or an `obsidian://` page link.

**Review focus:**

ENG-2227 reached the same conclusion on the Roam side.
- **The migration is load-bearing, not a nicety.** `T.linkUrl.optional()` would validate an absent key, but the eligibility gate is `'url' in props` — so without a backfill, pre-existing text shapes would silently never show **Edit link** while new ones would. Without the migration entirely, validation throws and `TldrawView` swallows it into a blank canvas.
- **The forked dialog is global, so it also serves geo shapes**, whose `url` prop is still stock `T.linkUrl`. `validateUrlForShape` keeps geo on the strict validator; letting an `obsidian://` URL through for a geo shape would throw at `updateShapes`. - **The protocol allowlist is a security boundary.** The affordance renders `<a href={url}>`, so admitting arbitrary protocols would make `javascript:` an XSS vector. It enumerates rather than falling through to "anything that parses".
- `baseShapeUtils` exists because the schema and the editor are built from **two separate arrays that nothing asserts agree** — update only one and you get either a throw on save or links that persist but never render.

**Risk / follow-up:**

<pr-created>https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1442</pr-created>

**The icon fix.** It now sits just past the text's right edge, vertically centred. Two things were going on:

- tldraw parks the icon in a geo shape's empty top-right corner, but a text shape is exactly as big as its text — so that corner *is* the text.
- My first attempt silently half-worked. `apps/obsidian/styles.css` is concatenated *ahead* of the vendored tldraw CSS, so a single-class rule ties on specificity and loses on source order. `left: 100%` only took effect by accident (tldraw sets `right`, not `left`); `top: 50%` was ignored outright. Scoping to `.tl-hyperlink-button.dg-text-hyperlink-button` fixed it. I have the picture. No changes made — here's the state and the plan.

## Where PR [#1442](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1442) stands

CI is **fully green**. It's blocked purely on `CHANGES_REQUESTED` from mdroidian — 3 unresolved comments, all landed 2026-09-22. Branch is **52 commits behind main**; only `styles.css` is touched on both sides and it looks auto-mergeable.

Head is now `eaaf6202`, two commits beyond what I pushed. A later session added `f45e008a` and `eaaf6202`, which fixed review finding #9 (the schema fallback). **All three of Michael's comments are on that work**, not on the link feature.

## The three comments, assessed honestly

**1. `canvasFileSync.ts:70` — "How is this related to adding link support on text shapes?"**

Fair, and I'd concede the framing. It isn't directly related; it's fallout. Making `url` *required* turned a previously-harmless missing-schema case into "canvas won't open". But here's the fact that matters: `createRawTldrawFile` (`tldraw.ts:112`) **always** writes `schema`. This plugin never produces a schema-less file. That path is reachable only via hand-editing, corruption, or a file written by the *other* tldraw-in-obsidian plugin — which `TldrawRawData`'s own comment says we deliberately follow.

**2. `tldraw.ts:57` — "Is this from tldraw docs or something Claude cooked up?"**

Cooked up. There's no tldraw doc for `schemaBeforeAppMigrations`. The *mechanism* is real and I verified it in-app earlier in this PR — retroactive sequences replay only when absent from the loaded schema, so listing them at current version makes `loadSnapshot` skip the backfill and the next `store.put` throws. But right now nothing pins that, which is exactly why the question is reasonable.

**3. `tldraw.ts:90` — "legacy?"**

He's right. The comment calls the stored schema "the legacy on-disk format"; it isn't legacy, it's just typed `unknown`. Sloppy wording, cheap reword.

## One thing that changed under us

`apps/obsidian` **on main now has Vitest** — `vitest.config.mts` and the exact scripts I removed at your request two weeks ago. Merging main brings it back for free (your branch's net package.json change is empty, so no conflict). That makes a test cheap, and a test is the strongest available answer to "cooked up?" — it converts the claim into a pinned invariant.

## The decision that drives everything

Whether to keep the schema-fallback work hinges on one thing I can't settle alone: **do we actually care about canvas files this plugin didn't write?** If tldraw-in-obsidian interop is real, schema-less files are plausible and the guard earns its place. If not, it's speculative defensive code on an already scope-stretched PR, and Michael's instinct is correct.

That condition has now fired, and Michael found it from the other direction.

**And one of my two reasons was wrong.** I said meta forces hand-rolling "the menu item and dialog". The dialog is needed either way — `T.linkUrl` rejects `obsidian://`, so the 214-line fork exists because of page-link support, not because of props-vs-meta. The real marginal cost of meta is only the menu item plus a gate hook, ~40 lines. So the argument I leaned on was roughly half as strong as I stated.

## What the research says now

Net code is **~60-70 lines lighter** under meta, not the big simplification Michael hopes for — a custom shape util is required either way, because the util is what renders the icon. On his actual framing, "reuses more of tldraw", meta is **backwards**: it forfeits all three stock menu entries.

But the decisive trade isn't line count, it's compatibility:

| | `props.url` (current) | `meta.url` |
|---|---|---|
| Old build opens a new file | `Unexpected property: url` → **blank canvas** | loads fine, ignores the link, **round-trips it intact on save** |
| Migration + schema-fallback plumbing | ~57 lines | **gone** — which also deletes the code Michael called "suspicious" |
| URL validation | enforced at load by the schema | only on write — needs a **render-time guard**, or `javascript:` in a hand-edited file reaches `<a href>` |

Canvas files are plain markdown synced between machines on different plugin versions, so the blank-canvas mode is the serious one. There's also direct precedent: `relationInstanceId` already lives in `shape.meta` in this plugin.

Two further findings worth knowing before you decide:

- **A patch is viable and cheap for the *validator*.** Patching `validLinkProtocols` in `@tldraw/validate@3.14.2` (2 files) makes `obsidian://` work for text *and* geo consistently, and fixes the stock dialog for free — which would let us delete our dialog fork. Michael's remembered embed-hostname patch is real but was deleted by the very next tldraw upgrade, so it survived exactly one version.
- **Click behaviour is genuinely inconsistent today**, and he's right to flag it. Discourse nodes: cmd+click → new tab, shift+click → sidebar. Our text link: cmd+click → **sidebar**. Same modifier, different destination.

My recommendation is to switch to `meta.url` — it answers his question, deletes the schema work he objected to, and fixes the rollback hazard — combined with the validator patch so the dialog fork goes too.

Yes — and it's the cheapest patch on the table. But two corrections to the premise.

**The line you linked doesn't exist in our version.** In 3.14.2, `utils/shapes/shapes.ts` contains only `getTextLabels`. That refactor is newer than what we ship.

## What a patch would actually touch in 3.14.2

The check is inline and duplicated across three logical sites (each ×2 for esm/cjs):

| Site | Purpose | Patchable for meta? |
|---|---|---|
| `menu-hooks.mjs:127` — `useHasLinkShapeSelected` | the eligibility gate | **yes, ~1 line** |
| `EditLinkDialog.mjs:27` | dialog's own guard — returns `null` | yes, but substantive |
| `EditLinkDialog.mjs:75` | writes `props: { url }` | yes, but substantive |

So patching **just the gate** — 2 files, one line each — makes **Edit link** appear in all three stock menus (context, main, actions) for a meta-based text shape, in tldraw's own position inside the Edit submenu. The stock *dialog* still won't work with meta, because it's separately gated and writes to props.

That's fine, though: **we need our own dialog regardless**, since `T.linkUrl` rejects `obsidian://`. Our `edit-link` action override already points the action at it.

**`meta.url` + gate patch** → no migration, no schema-fallback plumbing (the code Michael called suspicious disappears), no blank-canvas-on-rollback, *and* stock menu placement. It answers both halves of his comment at once — store in meta, and reuse stock components via a small patch, exactly the precedent he cited.

Still needed under that combo, unavoidably: the custom shape util (it's what renders the icon), the dialog fork, the vendored button (we need click interception so `obsidian:` never reaches the OS handler), and a **render-time URL guard** — because `meta` is `T.jsonValue`, nothing validates it at load, so a hand-edited file could otherwise put `javascript:` into an `<a href>`.

content.text:
## The dialog fork

`TextLinkDialog.tsx` — **214 lines**. tldraw doesn't export `EditLinkDialog` (zero hits in `dist-esm/index.d.mts`), so it's a near-verbatim copy of theirs: the input, the `https://` auto-prefix, the doubled-paste correction, the Clear/Save state machine. The only real change is `validateUrlForShape`, which accepts `obsidian://` for text shapes while keeping geo on tldraw's strict `T.linkUrl`.

## The vendored button

`HyperlinkButton` inside `TextShapeWithLinkUtil.tsx` — about 55 of its 121 lines. Also a copy, because `HyperlinkButton` isn't exported either. It reproduces tldraw's `<a class="tl-hyperlink-button">` markup so text links look identical to geo links, and adds two things tldraw's version doesn't have:

- `handleClick` — intercepts `obsidian:` hrefs and calls `preventDefault()`, so the URI never reaches the OS handler
- `stopUnlessShift` — tldraw's own trick so a plain click doesn't drag the shape, but shift still reaches the select tool

Worth noting for the patch discussion: **exporting them wouldn't delete either one.** The stock dialog is hard-wired to `T.linkUrl` and to `props`; the stock button takes no `onClick`, so we can't wrap it to add interception. An export-only patch is the smallest patch but buys the least. The thing that would actually delete the 214-line dialog is patching the *validator* — and only if we stay on `props`, since the stock dialog reads and writes props.

## On the render-time guard

Your instinct is half right, and the half that's wrong is the one that matters.

Validating in the dialog is worth doing — it's what disables Save and shows "Invalid URL". But it only covers values that arrive *through our dialog*. Under `meta`, nothing validates at load, and a value can reach `meta.url` by at least four other routes:

- a hand-edited canvas file — these are plain `.md` with a JSON block, which users edit and sync between machines
- a file written by an older or newer build, or another tool
- copy/paste or duplicate of a shape (meta is preserved through both — verified in the research)
- any future code path that writes meta without going through the dialog

The sink is `<a href={url}>` inside Electron. So `javascript:` in a hand-edited file would render as a live link with no UI ever having validated it.

That's precisely the safety net `props` gives us for free — the schema rejects a bad URL at load, which is why **no render guard is needed on the current `props` implementation**. Losing it is a real cost of moving to meta, and it belongs on the ledger alongside "no migration".

The fix is one line, reusing the function we already have:

```tsx
if (!isAllowedTextLinkUrl(url)) return null;
```

So: not either/or, and not much work. Dialog check for UX, sink check for safety.

Net, if we go meta + gate patch, the honest inventory is: custom shape util (~65 lines, needed either way to render the icon), vendored button (~55), dialog fork (214), render guard (1) — and we delete the migration, the schema-fallback plumbing, and the rollback hazard.

Checked both overlays — and there's an important wrinkle in the precedent.

**Both existing overlays are selection-scoped.** `RelationsOverlay` uses `getOnlySelectedShape()` (`RelationOverlay.tsx:22`), and so does `DragHandleOverlay` (`:102`). Neither iterates the page. So the pattern exists, but only for "one shape, recomputed on selection + camera change" — nobody here has done an always-on, per-shape overlay.

That said, **yes, this works, and it's the biggest simplification on the table.**

## What it buys

If the icon is an overlay, we never touch tldraw's text shape at all. Combined with `meta`, that deletes:

- `TextShapeWithLinkUtil` — 121 lines
- `baseShapeUtils` — 21 lines, *and* the "two lists that nothing asserts agree" hazard I had to write a comment about
- the migration, the schema-fallback plumbing, the swap assertion

Which leaves the dialog fork as the only sizeable custom piece. That is precisely the "reduce the amount of custom code we need to maintain" Michael asked for — far more so than meta alone.

## What it costs

The overlay sits above the canvas in viewport space, so four things that in-shape rendering gets for free become ours:

- **Rotation** — `getShapePageBounds` is axis-aligned, so on a rotated text shape the icon lands wrong. Geo's rotates with the shape. (Fixable with `getShapePageTransform`, but it's us doing it.)
- **Stacking** — the overlay draws above *every* shape, so a link icon would show through a shape stacked on top of its text.
- **Frame clipping** — a text shape clipped by a frame would still show its icon outside the frame.
- **Culling** — tldraw culls off-screen shapes automatically; an always-on overlay would recompute all linked shapes on every camera change. At realistic canvas sizes (a handful of links) this is a non-issue; I'd only flag it, not weight it.

## One design question it forces

Always-on or hover/selection-scoped?

- **Always-on** matches geo and keeps the icon as the *only* signal that a text shape is linked.
- **Hover-scoped** matches how Discourse nodes already work — their "Open in sidebar" button appears on hover (`DiscourseNodeShape.tsx:398`) — and sidesteps rotation/stacking/clipping almost entirely, since you'd only position one shape at a time.

These pull against each other, and it's exactly the tension in Michael's review: "mirror Discourse node behaviour" and "stay closer to the stock link UI" point in opposite directions here. The asymmetry that decides it for me: a Discourse node is *visibly* a node even without its hover button, whereas a linked text shape looks like plain text. Hover-only would make links undiscoverable.

**My recommendation: always-on overlay + `meta.url` + the 2-line gate patch.** That's no schema change, no migration, no custom shape util, stock menu item in its stock position, and the dialog fork as the one remaining copy. I'd accept the rotation/stacking/clipping edge cases and note them in the PR.

# ENG-2228 — Rework text-shape links: meta storage + overlay affordance

## Context

PR [#1442](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1442) is green on CI but sits at `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Michael asked us to stop and compare approaches before committing to a schema change, and left three inline objections — all of them on the schema-fallback plumbing (`canvasFileSync.ts:70`, `tldraw.ts:57`, `tldraw.ts:90`), not on the link feature.

His two substantive asks, and what the investigation found:

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify

# Obsidian CDP verify

## The one command

From the worktree root:

```sh
node ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/run.mjs \
  --slot 1 --marker "<string only this change's bundle contains>" \
  --scenario path/to/scenarios.mjs [--scenario more.mjs] [--port 9222] [--skip-build]
```

It runs doctor → launch → deliver → scenarios → cleanup and prints the `last-run.json` path, the scenario matrix, and the `pr-evidence` args. Exit codes: 0 all pass, 1 failure, 2 vault locked, 3 marker missing.

Write scenario files in the session scratchpad, not the repo.

## Launch

- Slots come from `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS` in `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env`. It takes a JSON array or a comma list of plugin dirs or vault roots. `--slot N` is 1-based and defaults to 1.
- If Obsidian is running on the debug port, the script attaches.
- If it's running without the port, the script quits Obsidian and relaunches it with `--remote-debugging-port`. Trang approved this; the windows come back.
- If it isn't running, the script launches it with the port.
- It then opens the slot vault through `obsidian://open?path=` and waits for a page target where `.workspace` exists and `app.vault.adapter.basePath` matches the vault.
- It writes the lock `<vault>/.obsidian/dg-verify.lock` (`{pid, branch, startedAt}`) and releases it in `finally`.

## Doctor

`scripts/doctor.mjs [--slot N]` is read-only and prints JSON: the resolved slot, the lock and the Obsidian state. If another live run holds the lock, it exits 2 and asks you to switch slot. A lock left by a dead pid is ignored.

## Deliver

`scripts/deliver.mjs --marker <str>` also runs on its own.

1. `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<slot plugin dir> tsx scripts/build.ts` runs once in `apps/obsidian`. It also writes `apps/obsidian/dist`, which is gitignored.
2. It greps the vault's `main.js` for `--marker` and fails if the marker is absent.
3. It reloads the plugin. The plugin id and folder are resolved from the manifests.
4. It greps again.
5. It warns about competing `dev.ts`/esbuild watchers. Your own worktree's watcher counts too, if it mirrors into the same vault.

The harness also hashes `main.js` before and after the scenarios. If it changed, the run is marked invalid.

## Drive: scenario contract

A module's `export default` is one scenario or an array of them:

```js
export default {
  name: "Search modal renders",                 // matrix row + screenshot name
  input: "run open-node-search",                // matrix text
  expected: "modal with a textbox and footer",  // matrix text
  setup: async (ctx) => ({ /* state; snapshot anything you change */ }),  // optional
  run: async ({ client, json, vault }, state) => {
    await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById(${json(`${vault.pluginId}:open-node-search`)});`);
    await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".dg-node-search-modal [role=textbox]")`);
    return client.evaluate(`document.querySelectorAll(".dg-search-footer-action").length`);
  },
  expect: (actual, state) => ({ pass: actual > 0, actual: `${actual} footer actions` }),  // or a boolean
  teardown: async (ctx, state) => {},           // optional: restore what setup changed
};
```

- `ctx` has `client`, `vault` (`root`, `pluginId`, `pluginDir`), `branch`, `json`, `verifyPath(name)` and `writeNote(name, body)`. `writeNote` creates or overwrites `_verify/<branch>/<name>` and returns its path.
- `client` has `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `pressEscape`, `screenshot`, `reloadPlugin`, `clearModals` and `send` (raw CDP).
- The harness does these for you:
  - Before each scenario, it clears modals and restores the layout captured at the start of the run.
  - After `run`, it takes a screenshot.
  - A thrown error becomes a failing row.
- The worked example is `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` (ENG-2114, 3 scenarios).

## Evidence

- The artifacts go to `<worktree>/local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/<branch>/<runStamp>/`: `<n>-<slug>.png` and `last-run.json` (`results[]` of `{scenario, input, expected, actual, pass, screenshot}`).
- Paste the printed matrix into create-pr's Evidence section.
- Upload the screenshots with pr-evidence, using the printed args:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts --harness obsidian-cdp <printed args>
```

## Cleanup

- Cleanup dismisses modals (Escape, then force-removes leftover `.modal-container`), restores the baseline layout and releases the lock.
- **It never deletes folders or notes.** `_verify/<branch>/` persists, and reruns overwrite its notes.
- Scenarios that change vault or app settings must restore them in `teardown`.

## Gotchas

These are the ones the code can't handle for you.

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| Double-handled keypress | Pass `type` to `client.key` only through its loop. Never send your own `keyDown`. |
| `editor.hasFocus()` false while focus looks right | This can't be measured over CDP. Assert the consequence instead, e.g. the cursor moved past the inserted text. |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks right | Saves are debounced (about 2s). `waitFor` on `app.vault.read(...)`, and don't read once. |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found" | Every markdown leaf was detached. Use `getLeaf("tab")`. |
| Top-level `await` throws in `evaluate` | Bodies run in a plain function. Return an async IIFE or a promise chain. |
| `iterateRootLeaves` count caps at 2 | A truthy callback return stops the iteration. Use a block body `{ n++; }`. |
| Escape handler in a modal child never wins | Obsidian's modal scope runs first. Push a `Scope` with `app.keymap.pushScope`. |
| Styling CodeMirror spans disappears on focus or scroll | Use a CM6 decoration, not MutationObserver stamping. A widget's `ignoreEvent()` must stay `true` for clicks. |
| Selectors from an old ENG example don't match | The UI drifts. The node search input is now a contenteditable `[role=textbox]`, not an `<input>`. |
| Flaky failure that looks like a code bug | Trang may be using the app mid-run. Rerun before believing a single observation. |
| Timers stall, writes land minutes late | Focus emulation normally prevents this. If it recurs, check `document.visibilityState` and ask Trang to show the window. |
| zsh eats `${VAR}` in `node -e` | Write scenarios to `.mjs` files. |

cd /Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/eng-2228-add-link-support-to-tldraw-text-shapes-in-obsidian
git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
Store text-shape links in meta and render them from an overlay

Michael asked us to compare meta.url against the props schema change before
committing to it, and to see how much stock tldraw we could reuse. Both point
the same way.

meta is validated as T.jsonValue, so existing canvases load untouched: the
migration, the schema fallback and its two call sites are gone, along with the
code flagged in review. The deciding argument is compatibility, not code volume
-- a file written with props.url and opened by an older build throws
Unexpected property and renders a blank canvas, while meta.url loads, is
ignored, and round-trips intact. Canvas files are markdown synced between
machines on different plugin versions, so that mattered more than keeping the
props-gated menu item for free.

Rendering the icon from InFrontOfTheCanvas, next to the existing Relations and
DragHandle overlays, means the stock text shape is never subclassed at all, so
the custom shape util and the two-shape-util-lists hazard go with it. The
trade is that the icon does not rotate with the shape, is not clipped by a
frame, and draws above shapes stacked over the text.

A two-line patch keeps tldraw's own Edit link item: useHasLinkShapeSelected
gates on 'url' in props, so it now also accepts text shapes -- always, the way
geo qualifies through a props.url that defaults to "". Gating on the presence
of meta.url instead would have made the first link unaddable.

Click gestures now match discourse nodes: plain opens the sidebar, cmd opens a
new tab, cmd+alt splits. Since meta is unvalidated, the URL allowlist is
re-applied when reading it rather than relying on the schema.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
MSG
